chunks: Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"When ten years have passed for the boy, then whatever he frees and gives in charity in a good manner from his wealth is valid."

key_terms.أَعْتَقَ: He freed, referring to manumission of a slave
key_terms.الْغُلَامِ: The boy/son, referring to a male child under puberty
key_terms.عَشْرُ سِنِينَ: Ten years, the specific age threshold mentioned for legal capacity
key_terms.وَجْهِ الْمَعْرُوفِ: In a good/approved manner, a standard legal phrase indicating propriety
key_terms.يَجُوزُ: Is valid/permissible, indicating legal acceptance of the action

ai.seo_question: At what age is a boy's financial transactions like freeing slaves and giving charity considered legally valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the Shia jurisprudential tradition, this hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the age of ten as the threshold for limited legal capacity (ahliyyat al-adā’) in financial transactions, distinguishing it from full maturity. It confirms that a boy’s acts of manumission and charity are valid provided they are executed in a 'proper manner' (al-ma'rūf), reflecting the principle that financial competence is recognized before full physical maturity, a key point in Usuli debates on the age of bulugh.
